Hooks & Events ​

Extensions subscribe to hooks in extension.json and register listeners in activate().

Lifecycle ​

HookDescription
on:app:readyApp initialized, safe to access core APIs
on:app:shutdownApp shutting down, flush pending data
on:config:changeExtension config changed

Shares ​

HookDescriptionPayload
before:share:createCan block with { block: true, reason }name, visibility, recipients
after:share:createShare was createdshareId, name, visibility, recipients
after:share:revokeShare was revokedshareId

Transfers ​

HookDescriptionPayload
before:download:startCan block downloadsname, magnetUri
after:download:completeTransfer finishedsize, duration, speed, filePath, name

Peers ​

HookDescriptionPayload
on:peer:connectPeer connectedhandle, publicKey
on:peer:disconnectPeer disconnectedhandle, publicKey
on:auth:loginUser authenticatedhandle

Billing ​

HookDescriptionPayload
after:billing:upgradePlan upgradedplan
after:billing:downgradePlan downgradedreason

Blocking Hooks ​

Hooks prefixed with before: can prevent the action by returning { block: true, reason }:

js
ctx.hooks.on('before:share:create', async ({ name, visibility }) => {
  if (visibility === 'global') {
    return { block: true, reason: 'Global shares are disabled by policy' };
  }
});

ctx.hooks.on('before:download:start', async ({ name }) => {
  if (name.endsWith('.exe')) {
    return { block: true, reason: 'Executable downloads are blocked' };
  }
});

INFO

Errors in hook handlers are caught and logged — they don't prevent other listeners from running.

Registering Hooks ​

Declare hooks in your manifest, then register in activate():

json
{
  "hooks": ["on:app:ready", "after:share:create", "after:download:complete"]
}
js
export function activate(ctx) {
  ctx.hooks.on('on:app:ready', async () => {
    ctx.logger.info('App is ready');
  });

  ctx.hooks.on('after:share:create', async ({ shareId, name }) => {
    ctx.logger.info(`Share created: ${name}`);
  });
}
